title: Ebola 2026
text: May 2026, Democratic Republic Congo (DRC) reported Ebola outbreak caused Bundibugyo strain, five months previous epidemic. July 2026, 2,423 cases 967 deaths reported. Rapid forecasting critical guiding public health response resource allocation. vignette demonstrates use incast forecast Ebola incidence using surveillance data Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB). vignette executed models computationally expensive. Running code locally may take several minutes.

title: Ebola 2026
text: model six locations highest cumulative confirmed cases. location, create daily time series latest reporting date, filling missing days carrying forward cumulative counts removing downward corrections. Leading zeros first reported case removed models use log-transformed incidence; locations later introductions therefore shorter time series.
code: library(dplyr) library(tidyr) library(ggplot2)  ebola <- read.csv(   "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scc-usc/ebola2026/refs/heads/main/hubverse_observed_data.csv" ) |>   filter(     target == "insp_sitrep__cumulative_confirmed_cases__daily",     !is.na(location)   ) |>   mutate(target_end_date = as.Date(target_end_date))  top_locations <- ebola |>   slice_max(target_end_date, by = location) |>   slice_max(observation, n = 6) |>   pull(location)  ebola <- ebola |>   filter(location %in% top_locations) |>   arrange(location, target_end_date) |>   group_by(location) |>   complete(     target_end_date = seq(       min(target_end_date),       max(target_end_date),       by = "day"     )   ) |>   fill(observation, .direction = "down") |> # carry cumulative over gaps   mutate(observation = cummax(coalesce(observation, 0))) |> # monotonic, per location   filter(cumsum(observation > 0) > 0) |> # drop pre-first-case zeros; log() needs > 0   ungroup() |>   mutate(target = "insp_sitrep__cumulative_confirmed_cases__daily")

title: Ebola 2026
text: check_data() validates Ebola data returns incast_data object. function checks missing values, ensures data correct format, verifies necessary columns present.  Revised history cumulative confirmed cases available outbreak, skip get_ncast() proceed directly cross-validation forecasting.
code: library(incast) data <- ebola |> check_data() data #> <incast_data> #> Target:   insp_sitrep__cumulative_confirmed_cases__daily #> Series:   6 (location) #> Window:   2026-05-15 to 2026-07-26 (1-day interval) data |> autoplot()

title: Ebola 2026
text: get_cv() performs rolling-origin time series cross-validation returns incast_cv object containing results model location. First define list models test. use default models provided incast fable add custom models, including ARIMA, neural network, several foundation models. forecast 7 days ahead 16 origins spaced 1 day apart, evaluation period spans 22 days.  autoplot() summarises cross-validation performance using relative WIS (wis_relative_skill cv$score). Raw WIS depends scale observed data therefore directly comparable across locations. Relative WIS normalises scores within location, allowing performance compared across locations. log scale makes relative differences easier interpret: values 0.5 2 indicate half double reference WIS, respectively, equally distant reference value 1 log scale. can also build summaries cv$score. example, raw WIS per model location.
code: library(fable) library(fable.prophet)  models <- c(   default_models(),   list(     CUSTOM_ARIMA = ARIMA(log(observation) ~ pdq(1, 1, 0)),     NNETAR = NNETAR(log(observation), n_networks = 10),     PROPHET = prophet(log(observation)),     # you will need a python environment (see reticulate)     CHRONOS = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "chronos"),     TIMESFM = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "timesfm"),     SUNDIAL = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "sundial"),     MOIRAI = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "moirai")   ) ) cv <- data |>   get_cv(     h = 7, # forecast horizon     step = 1, # one origin per day     n_origins = 16,     models = models   ) cv #> <incast_cv> #> Target:   insp_sitrep__cumulative_confirmed_cases__daily #> Series:   6 (location) #> Window:   2026-05-15 to 2026-07-26 (1-day interval) #> CV:       11 models x 16 origins (h = 7) cv |>   autoplot() +   ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(transform = "log2") cv$score |>   group_by(location) |>   arrange(wis, .by_group = TRUE) |>   mutate(model_id_ordered = paste(model_id, location, sep = "__")) |>   ggplot(aes(y = reorder(model_id_ordered, wis), x = wis)) +   facet_wrap(~location, scales = "free") +   geom_col(aes(fill = model_id), show.legend = FALSE) +   scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) sub("__.*$", "", x)) +   theme_classic() +   labs(y = "Model", x = "WIS")

title: Ebola 2026
text: default get_fcast() use best 3 model location based cross-validation results. function returns incast_fcast object containing forecasts location. autoplot() visualizes ensemble forecasts location, including median, 50% 95% prediction intervals.  can also build plot using as_tibble() extract forecast data ggplot2 create custom visualization.
code: fcast <- cv |> get_fcast() fcast #> <incast_fcast> #> Target:   insp_sitrep__cumulative_confirmed_cases__daily #> Series:   6 (location) #> Forecast: 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-02 (h = 7) #> Models:   9 + ENSEMBLE fcast$meta$selection #> # A tibble: 18 × 2 #>    location  model_id     #>    <chr>     <chr>        #>  1 Bunia     SUNDIAL      #>  2 Bunia     TIMESFM      #>  3 Bunia     MOIRAI       #>  4 Katwa     NNETAR       #>  5 Katwa     MOIRAI       #>  6 Katwa     PROPHET      #>  7 Lita      PROPHET      #>  8 Lita      THETA        #>  9 Lita      ARIMA        #> 10 Mongbwalu MOIRAI       #> 11 Mongbwalu NNETAR       #> 12 Mongbwalu SUNDIAL      #> 13 Nizi      ETS          #> 14 Nizi      ARIMA        #> 15 Nizi      CUSTOM_ARIMA #> 16 Rwampara  SUNDIAL      #> 17 Rwampara  TIMESFM      #> 18 Rwampara  NNETAR fcast |> autoplot() fcast |>   as_tibble() |>   ggplot() +   geom_ribbon(     aes(x = target_end_date, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = model_id),     alpha = 0.2,     show.legend = FALSE   ) +   geom_line(     aes(x = target_end_date, y = median, colour = model_id),     show.legend = TRUE   ) +   facet_wrap(~location, scales = "free") +   # ground truth   geom_line(     data = fcast$hub$oracle_output |>       filter(target_end_date >= as.Date("2026-07-01")),     aes(x = target_end_date, y = oracle_value),     color = "black"   ) +   theme_classic() +   theme(     legend.position = "bottom",     legend.title = element_blank()   )

title: Forecasting connected time series with HHH4
text: incast models forecast series separately. HHH4 fits series together, allowing recent counts one series help predict another. unit one value series key, one state key = "location". HHH4 requires single key column meaningful set connected units.

title: Forecasting connected time series with HHH4
text: HHH4 models expected count sum three components: expected count=endemic+autoregressive+neighbour. \text{expected count} = \text{endemic} + \text{autoregressive} + \text{neighbour}. example uses settings: S = 1 one seasonal harmonic: sine/cosine pair learns timing size repeating annual cycle.

title: Forecasting connected time series with HHH4
text: example forecasts weekly influenza hospital admissions Connecticut, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania. code run vignette built get_data() uses live API.

title: Forecasting connected time series with HHH4
text: HHH4 needs one count target, one series key, aligned reporting dates. external data, use check_data(data, key = "location").
code: # install.packages("surveillance") # Run once if needed. library(incast) library(surveillance)  states <- c("ct", "nj", "ny", "pa") flu <- get_data(pathogen = "flu", geo_value = states)  autoplot(flu)

title: Forecasting connected time series with HHH4
text: Rows connection matrix sources columns receiving units. , 1 means two states share border. Population used offset, allowing larger states larger background count. names must match series key values exactly.
code: adjacency <- rbind(   CT = c(CT = 0, NJ = 0, NY = 1, PA = 0),   NJ = c(CT = 0, NJ = 0, NY = 1, PA = 1),   NY = c(CT = 1, NJ = 1, NY = 0, PA = 1),   PA = c(CT = 0, NJ = 1, NY = 1, PA = 0) )  population <- c(   CT = 3.6e6,   NJ = 9.5e6,   NY = 20.0e6,   PA = 13.0e6 ) population <- population / sum(population)

title: Forecasting connected time series with HHH4
text: First define one annual cycle endemic component: compare four component structures: Create four incast model specifications:
code: annual_seasonality <- addSeason2formula(   f = ~1,   S = 1,   period = round(365.25 / flu$interval) ) # Endemic only. end_control <- list(   ar = list(f = ~ -1),   ne = list(f = ~ -1),   end = list(f = annual_seasonality),   family = "NegBin1" )  # Autoregressive + endemic. ar_end_control <- end_control ar_end_control$ar <- list(f = ~1, lag = 1)  # Neighbour + endemic. ne_end_control <- end_control ne_end_control$ne <- list(f = ~1, lag = 1, normalize = TRUE)  # Full HHH4. full_control <- ar_end_control full_control$ne <- ne_end_control$ne hhh4_models <- list(   HHH4_END = HHH4(     observation,     control = end_control,     population = population   ),   HHH4_AR_END = HHH4(     observation,     control = ar_end_control,     population = population   ),   HHH4_NE_END = HHH4(     observation,     control = ne_end_control,     neighbourhood = adjacency,     population = population   ),   HHH4_FULL = HHH4(     observation,     control = full_control,     neighbourhood = adjacency,     population = population   ) )

title: Forecasting connected time series with HHH4
text: Compare HHH4 specifications default incast models using forecast origins: Passing hhh4_models get_fcast() refits forecasts four specifications. default plot shows ensemble; use model inspect specification.
code: models <- c(default_models(), hhh4_models)  set.seed(2026) cv <- get_cv(   flu,   h = 4,   eval_start_date = as.Date("2024-09-01"),   models = models )  autoplot(cv) set.seed(2026) fcast <- get_fcast(cv, models = hhh4_models)  autoplot(fcast) autoplot(fcast, model = "HHH4_END") autoplot(fcast, model = "HHH4_AR_END") autoplot(fcast, model = "HHH4_NE_END") autoplot(fcast, model = "HHH4_FULL")

title: Forecasting connected time series with HHH4
text: HHH4 separate formula component, add covariate component affects supply values control$data. example, school holidays may affect background incidence, add endemic component: simple example treats July August school holidays. Time-varying covariates must cover observed history forecast horizon. See ?surveillance::hhh4 component formulas, lags, covariates, distributions, weights, random effects, optimizer options.
code: h <- 4L dates <- seq(   min(flu$data$target_end_date),   max(flu$data$target_end_date) + h * flu$interval,   by = flu$interval ) school_holiday <- as.integer(format(dates, "%m") %in% c("07", "08"))  holiday_control <- full_control holiday_control$end$f <- addSeason2formula(   f = ~ 1 + school_holiday,   S = 1,   period = round(365.25 / flu$interval) ) holiday_control$data <- list(school_holiday = school_holiday)  hhh4_models$HHH4_SCHOOL_HOLIDAY <- HHH4(   observation,   control = holiday_control,   neighbourhood = adjacency,   population = population )

title: incast
text: recent weeks surveillance data almost always low hospitals still filing late reports (right truncated). feed raw counts forecaster, predictions biased downward. get_ncast() estimates recent counts look like reports arrive. default max_delay = 2, last 2 weeks corrected; everything left untouched.  corrected ncast$data contains two extra columns: ncast_lower ncast_upper (95% CrI) corrected weeks. get_fcast() detects automatically uses propagate nowcasting uncertainty final forecast.
code: ncast <- get_ncast(df) ncast #> <incast_ncast> #> Target:   wk inc flu hosp #> Series:   2 (location) #> Window:   2022-06-04 to 2025-12-13 (7-day interval) #> Nowcast:  2025-12-06 to 2025-12-13 autoplot(ncast)

title: incast
text: Forecasting split two steps: get_cv() (model selection): performs time series cross-validation full (median-corrected). Models ranked Weighted Interval Score (WIS). get_fcast() (final forecast): ensembles best top_n models generates forecasts h weeks ahead. nowcast columns available, forecasts generated lower, median, upper nowcast estimates pooled, prediction intervals capture model nowcast uncertainty. Default models : NAIVE: Carries last observed value forward. simple baseline. ETS (Exponential Smoothing): weighted average recent weeks matter older ones. Adapts trends seasonal patterns. THETA: Splits data long-term trend short-term fluctuations, forecasts separately, combines . ARIMA: Models temporal dependence series using autoregressive moving average terms. Parameters selected automatically.

title: incast
text: get_cv() performs rolling-origin time series cross-validation. Three arguments determine cross-validation performed. h: forecast horizon, , number reporting intervals predict ahead. step: spacing forecast origins. step = h (default) produces non-overlapping forecasts fastest option. step < h produces overlapping forecasts, resulting evaluation points requiring model fits. n_origins eval_start_date: evaluation period starts. Supply exactly one: n_origins: number forecast origins. eval_start_date: date first forecast origin. forecast origin time d predicts intervals d d + h - 1, n_origins origins spaced step intervals apart cover last h + (n_origins - 1) * step reporting intervals series. example, h = 4, step = 4, n_origins = 3, evaluation period covers last 12 intervals: Increasing n_origins provides reliable comparison models, leaves less historical data training. Ensure time series contains enough observations first forecast origin fit models reliably. function returns incast_cv object containing cross-validation results model location. Plot relative WIS model location using autoplot(). Values wis_relative_skill 1 indicate better--average forecasts (lower WIS), values 1 indicate worse--average forecasts (higher WIS).
code: Forecast 1: [d,   d+1, d+2,  d+3] Forecast 2: [d+4, d+5, d+6,  d+7] Forecast 3: [d+8, d+9, d+10, d+11] cv <- get_cv(ncast, h = 4, n_origins = 16) cv #> <incast_cv> #> Target:   wk inc flu hosp #> Series:   2 (location) #> Window:   2022-06-04 to 2025-12-13 (7-day interval) #> CV:       4 models x 16 origins (h = 4) autoplot(cv)

title: incast
text: get_fcast() ensembles best top_n models cross-validation forecasts h reporting intervals ahead. h defaults horizon used get_cv(). Plot ensemble forecast autoplot(fcast) (pass model = inspect single model instead):
code: fcast <- get_fcast(cv, top_n = 2) fcast #> <incast_fcast> #> Target:   wk inc flu hosp #> Series:   2 (location) #> Forecast: 2025-12-20 to 2026-01-10 (h = 4) #> Models:   3 + ENSEMBLE autoplot(fcast)

title: incast
text: model compatible fable framework can passed get_cv()/get_fcast() via models. Compose default_models() keep built-ins alongside :
code: library(fable) library(fable.prophet) library(EpiEstim) library(projections) my_models <- c(   default_models(),   list(     CUSTOM_ARIMA = ARIMA(observation ~ pdq(1, 1, 0)),     PROPHET = prophet(observation ~ season("year")),     NNETAR = NNETAR(observation),     EPIESTIM = EPIESTIM(observation, mean_si = 3, std_si = 2, rt_window = 7),     CHRONOS = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "chronos"),     TIMESFM = FOUNDATION(log(observation), "timesfm")   ) )  cv <- get_cv(   ncast,   n_origins = 16,   models = my_models )  fcast <- get_fcast(cv, top_n = 3)

title: EpiEstim model for fable — EPIESTIM
text: formula Response variable model, example observation. External predictors supported. mean_si Mean serial interval days. std_si Standard deviation serial interval days. rt_window Length sliding window (days) used estimate Rt. Smaller values respond quickly recent changes, larger values provide smoother estimates. Defaults 14. n_sim Number simulated forecast trajectories. Defaults 100. R_fix_within Logical indicating whether Rt held constant within simulated trajectory. Recommended short forecast horizons.

title: Forecast with a pretrained time-series model — FOUNDATION
text: Forecasts returned format fable models, allowing used functions get_cv get_fcast. models run Python using reticulate. first forecast session, required Python dependencies model weights installed downloaded automatically. cached subsequent forecasts. Available models (backend): "chronos" Amazon Chronos. Default: amazon/chronos-t5-small. "timesfm" Google TimesFM. Default: google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch. "sundial" Tsinghua Sundial. Default: thuml/sundial-base-128m. "moirai" Salesforce Moirai. Default: Salesforce/moirai-1.1-R-small. models provide limited number quantiles, extreme prediction intervals may approximate.

title: Cross-validate forecasting models — get_cv
text: Evaluate forecasting models using expanding-window time-series cross-validation. Starting eval_start_date, models refitted forecast origin evaluated next h time steps.

title: Cross-validate forecasting models — get_cv
code: get_cv(   x,   eval_start_date = NULL,   h = 4,   models = default_models(),   step = h,   n_origins = NULL )

title: Cross-validate forecasting models — get_cv
text: x incast_ncast object get_ncast incast_data object check_data get_data. eval_start_date Date (character string coercible date) giving first forecast origin evaluate. Must fall within data window. earlier observations used initial training period. argument exclusive n_origins. h Integer giving forecast horizon reporting intervals (example, weeks weekly data). Defaults 4. models Named list fable joint incast model specifications, HHH4. Defaults default_models. step Integer giving number reporting intervals successive cross-validation origins. Defaults h, resulting non-overlapping evaluation periods. n_origins Integer giving number forecast origins evaluate, alternative eval_start_date. Origins placed last forecast ends last observation: eval_start_date = t - ((h - 1) + (n_origins - 1) * step) * interval, t last observation date. argument exclusive eval_start_date.

title: Cross-validate forecasting models — get_cv
text: incast_cv object containing: forecasts Forecasts model, series, cross-validation origin. oracle Observed values used scoring. score Model performance metrics, including WIS interval coverage, model series. models evaluated model specifications. meta Cross-validation settings including dates, horizon, step, number origins, series keys, target, reporting interval. data Input data revisions collapsed, used get_fcast.

text: x incast_* object. models Named list ordinary fable joint incast model specifications, HHH4. Defaults default_models. x incast_cv object, leave unset use top-ranked models cross-validation, provide custom set models. h Integer giving forecast horizon reporting intervals. title: Nowcast right-truncated surveillance data — get_ncast
text: Recent weeks surveillance data incomplete reporting delays (right truncation). get_ncast estimates final counts baselinenowcast, replacing last max_delay weeks every series leaving earlier weeks untouched. Downward revisions redistributed across earlier delays via preprocess_negative_values.

title: Nowcast right-truncated surveillance data — get_ncast

Number posterior samples. Default 1000. prop_delay Numeric (0, 1). Proportion reference times used delay estimation. Default 0.5. scale_factor Numeric. Multiplier max_delay estimation window. Default 3.
